title: introduce token-choreography auth shim + compact retry presets + ergonomic stream viewbridge
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a lightweight token choreography shim across Py/TS/Go SDKs; introduces compact retry preset generator and a stabilized stream viewbridge API for ergonomic async iteration; bumps SDKs: python v1.28.0, typescript v1.18.0, go v1.12.3.
description:
Summary: Adds a small, language-agnostic 'token choreography' shim to harmonize credential handoffs across SDKs, introduces a compact retry-preset generator for common retry shapes, and stabilizes the stream viewbridge API (pull-oriented ergonomic iterator) with backward-compatible shims. Motivation: customer workloads combining long-lived resumable streams and delegated auth were showing fragile reauth windows and complex client wiring. This PR reduces application-level plumbing by centralizing minimal choreography semantics and providing easy retry presets tuned for streaming use-cases.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-3145) and implementation PoC for Python/TS/Go
- [x] End-to-end smoke tests for streaming resume + reauth in CI
- [x] Telemetry hooks for reauth events and retry counts
- [x] SDK version bumps and changelogs updated
- [x] Minimal migration guide added to SDK docs

Commits (summary):
- feat: introduce token choreography interface and minimal state machine (py/ts/go)
- feat: compact retry preset generator and presets file with conservative and aggressive profiles
- feat: stream viewbridge: introduce PullStreamView abstraction and TypeScript async iterator wrapper
- fix: ensure reauth backoff does not leak goroutines in Go connector
- test: add integration tests to cover resumption, fallback to alternate creds, and retry saturation
- docs: add HOWTO for streaming+delegated auth and upgrade notes

Files/areas changed (high level):
- sdk/python/redwood/session/choreography.py (new shim, adapter for existing SessionManager)
- sdk/typescript/src/stream/viewbridge.ts (PullStreamView + adapters)
- sdk/go/connector/cred_choreography.go (lightweight choreography and goroutine guards)
- sdk/common/retry/presets.yaml (new presets and generator script)
- examples/streaming/auth-handshake/ (updated quickstart for streaming with delegated tokens)
- docs/sdk/migrations/streaming-auth.md (migration notes)
- ci/integration/streaming-auth.yml (new matrix for py/ts/go smoke tests)

Review conversation (high level):
- Arjun: "Nice consolidation. Two asks: add a small benchmark for reauth latency and please call out memory/goroutine guard in Go tests."
- Maya: "Added benchmark harness and extended Go integration test to assert <2 goroutine leak over 30s; pushed new commit c4f2a8c."
- Lena: "API surface looks good. For TS, can we provide a tiny example of using PullStreamView with existing generator-based consumers?"
- Maya: "Added example in examples/streaming/auth-handshake/ts-example.md and updated README."
- Diego: "CI flakes on old node versions; recommend dropping unsupported Node 12 job."
- Maya: "Removed Node 12 from ci matrix and re-ran. All CI green."
- Arjun (approval): "Approved after small nits fixed. Good telemetry and docs coverage."

CI summary: Initial run: lint failures in TS (edge case with eslint rule), fixed in second commit. Integration matrix: python 3.10/3.11, node 14/16, go 1.20; all integration smoke tests passed on rerun. Telemetry unit tests recorded expected counters (reauth_attempts, retry_applied, stream_resumed).

Compatibility and migration notes: The token choreography shim is opt-in by default for existing SDK consumers (old SessionManager behavior unchanged). New constructors expose an optional choreography boolean flag; migration guide outlines the 2-line change to opt-in. PullStreamView is additive; we provide a small compatibility adapter PullStreamAdapter that maps previous callback-style streams to the new iterator surface. Retry presets are additive and referenced by name (e.g., "compact-conservative", "compact-aggressive").

Performance and safety: Benchmarks show median reauth latency improvement from 120ms to 45ms in typical cloud deployments (choreography avoids double-refresh races), and a 7% reduction in end-to-end token overhead in canonical streaming scenario. Go changes include guard rails to prevent goroutine accumulation during tight retry loops.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main. Changelog entries generated for each SDK. Tagging: python v1.28.0, typescript v1.18.0, go v1.12.3. Release PRs created to cut packages and update examples repo.

Follow-ups (planned):
- ENG-3199: Integrate token choreography telemetry into Console for per-key drift alerts
- Add an option to the retry generator to produce a 'low-latency' preset tuned for low-token-count, interactive sessions
- Monitor field telemetry for first 48h after release and prepare patch if any stream regressions are observed

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the choreography state machine simple (three states: fresh, leased, refreshing) to make audits and reasoning trivial; more advanced token multiplexing will be considered in a follow-up if telemetry indicates need.
